findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&`, denying team admins who are not owners even though either role should authorize the action.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70 — Submitted email addresses are not lowercased before comparison, allowing mixed-case input to bypass `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — Calendar updates use the acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's integration, potentially leaving the organizer's calendar unsynchronized after the database update.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — The server does not deduplicate addresses within `guests`, so repeated emails can be inserted multiple times by `createMany`.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees submitted with new guests to receive new-booking confirmations.
packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525 — Guest-addition emails ignore the event type's host and attendee standard-email suppression settings, causing disabled notifications to be sent.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:34 — Initializing the form with `[""]` leaves Add enabled for invalid empty input, so submitting the untouched dialog displays a misleading uniqueness/validity error instead of treating it as empty.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — Calendar updates use the acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's integration, potentially leaving the organizer's calendar unsynchronized after the database update.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in addGuests.handler.ts, line 158 shows `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` where ctx.user is the acting user (the person adding guests), not necessarily the organizer. Then at line 160-163, the EventManager is created with these credentials: `const eventManager = new EventManager({...user, credentials: [...credentials]});`. This means if an attendee or team admin adds guests, the calendar update will use their credentials instead of the organizer's. The booking object does include `booking.user.credentials` (from the include at line 38-41), which would be the organizer's credentials, but this is not used. This is a real bug - the calendar event should be updated using the organizer's calendar integration, not the acting user's.
